brief: A Market Ear roundup frames the AI trade as at a decision point. Nvidia fell to its major trendline, now 22% below its 200-day average versus 30% at the Liberation Day lows, and NDX was rejected at its own 200-day with 27k the pivot level, as vol-control and risk-parity funds sold over $30bn in a week (JPM, GS, LSEG Workspace). JPM argues Nvidia is cheap despite the drop: it captured 83% of 2023-2025 AI chip revenue at 75% gross and 66% operating margins, now trading at a 0.2x PEG. GS adds that AI semis trade at 11x 2028 earnings versus 16x for the S&P 500 despite 31% forecast growth, implying either an earnings collapse or excess pessimism, with momentum shorts in NDX now vulnerable to a squeeze and systematic funds possible buyers by December/January if vol settles. Separately, DB's Sachdeva says Asian chip surpluses are recycling into US equities rather than Treasuries, feeding dollar strength, resistance at 105, but tying the dollar's fate to AI. GS sees Europe's near-zero AI beta as an emerging diversification trade.
